$Comment: What Enchanting means at the Greater Disenchanting Table: what it means at the lesser one, plus the queue's own pay. The greater table runs its own action, Disenchant_Greater (a child of the jar's Disenchant), and an extension's additions never flow down a Parent chain, so the lesser table's DisenchantingProgression.json cannot reach it. This file is a Parent child of that one and authors Target, the scoped {Station: Disenchanting_Table_Greater, Action: Disenchant_Greater}, and Bonus; every other leaf (the XP, the scale, the pace ladder with its Clamp and Stretch, and every table technique: the Recipe overlay, the StepOverlays and the inserted payout beats) is inherited from it, so each piece's ritual runs as long here, and each technique works the same way, as at the lesser table. Each queued piece is one cycle, so all three sockets pay. Bonus.Lootables replaces the inherited list whole, so it names the lesser table's tables again and adds the greater table's own: Mmo_Disenchant_Queue_Talents, what the trees' Greater Table stat pays on each queued piece; Mmo_Disenchant_Greater_Void, the jar's extra Void essence chance (moved out of this pack's Disenchant_Greater_Bonus copy so Kit Rite can shut it); and Mmo_Disenchant_Greater_Rites, Void Rite and Treasure Hunter rolling that chance again. A table added to the lesser list belongs here too. To tune the two tables apart, author the leaf you want different here and it replaces the inherited one.
